cases.terminal: By 1799 a fixed-wing concept separated lift, propulsion and control, and by 1804 a model glider flew. Powered flight did not follow for decades.
cases.lineage: The conceptual decomposition was useful, but engines, materials and control capabilities adequate for powered flight were still missing. The representation arrived before the full intervention path became tractable.
cases.question: A team now has the correct high-level decomposition and a working unpowered model but cannot realize the powered target. What is the strongest next reachability move?

actions.A: Keep refining the conceptual decomposition until powered flight follows from representation alone.
actions.B: Treat the target as blocked by missing complementary capability and search/acquire the load-bearing power-to-weight, materials and control relations.
actions.C: Classify the target as physically impossible because the correct representation has not yet produced a powered realization.
actions.D: Preserve only the final glider result; earlier decomposition and missing-capability lineage are irrelevant to next-step selection.

cases.terminal: Spectroscopy became a method for identifying elements and inferring celestial composition from light.
cases.lineage: Chemists needed low-concentration identification and astronomers could not sample celestial material. Gross flame color was insufficiently discriminating. A slit/prism spectroscope, clean flame source, calibration/reference samples and stable line identities turned light into a repeatable chemical representation; this revealed new elements and made remote composition empirically addressable. Wet chemistry remained important for confirmation.
cases.question: The target is currently unanswerable because the object cannot be sampled directly and existing observations collapse rival compositions. What is the strongest next reachability move?

actions.A: Search harder inside the existing observation basis; no new instrument or representation is needed.
actions.B: Construct or acquire a more discriminating observation channel and calibration/reference system that can separate the rival worlds, then validate the mapping to the target claim.
actions.C: Treat physical inaccessibility of the sample as proof that composition is epistemically unreachable in principle.
actions.D: Replace empirical work with a more detailed theoretical model and treat its prediction as the composition result.

cases.terminal: An extreme-scale steamship struggled in its intended passenger/commercial role; later it was used for cable laying.
cases.lineage: The project failed or underperformed its declared commercial objective while proving unusual scale/capacity capabilities. Under a later problem, those retained physical capabilities became valuable as a cable-laying platform. HD2-N2 classifies this as latent option value after declared-objective failure, without reclassifying the original commercial result as success.
cases.question: A capability-bearing artifact has failed its original objective and a materially different target appears later. What is the strongest reachability decision?

actions.A: Delete the artifact and its reconstruction lineage because original-objective failure proves zero future capability value.
actions.B: Keep the original failure standing, but re-evaluate the artifact's reusable capabilities against the new target and retain only the justified reconstruction/option path.
actions.C: Rewrite the original project as a success because a later use was found.
actions.D: Keep every failed artifact active indefinitely because unknown future goals make all carrying costs worthwhile.

cases.terminal: Containerization transformed freight through standardized intermodal containers and specialized handling.
cases.lineage: The metal box alone was insufficient. End-to-end viability required cranes, purpose-built ships, truck chassis, rail cars, terminals, scheduling, customs procedures, capital and interoperable dimensions/corner fittings/testing. Early incompatible carrier-specific sizes risked fragmentation; ISO coordination reduced proprietary lock-in and made distributed equipment investment composable.
cases.question: A local prototype works, but cross-organization deployment is blocked because independently capable carriers cannot interoperate. What is the strongest next reachability move?

actions.A: Optimize the local artifact further and assume interoperability will emerge automatically from better local performance.
actions.B: Identify the load-bearing interface/standard and complementary infrastructure needed to compose the carriers into an end-to-end path; validate total-route performance.
actions.C: Conclude that the target requires one owner to vertically integrate every carrier before it can be reachable.
actions.D: Treat publication of a standard as proof that the distributed capability is already realized and current.

cases.terminal: The Scribner shunt helped turn dialysis into a chronic treatment and supported outpatient dialysis centers.
cases.lineage: Dialysis could already function as an acute/one-off intervention. The missing repeated vascular-access capability prevented durable chronic treatment. The 1960 Scribner shunt changed the treatment basis by enabling repeated access; durable service then also required an outpatient treatment system rather than the dialysis principle alone.
cases.question: A process succeeds once but repeated use is blocked by destructive or costly re-entry. What is the strongest next reachability move?

actions.A: Optimize the one-shot process while leaving re-entry/reuse unchanged.
actions.B: Treat repeatable access/re-entry and the surrounding service system as independent load-bearing capabilities and construct/validate them.
actions.C: Infer that because one-shot execution works, durable repeated capability is already established.
actions.D: Infer that repeated capability is impossible because current re-entry destroys the access path.

cases.terminal: The relational model and SQL became a dominant database abstraction.
cases.lineage: Codd's logical relations/data-independence idea did not itself establish practical performance. System R, SQL, cost-based optimization, indexes, transactions/recovery, storage management and statistics made declarative queries operational at acceptable cost. High-level representation and hidden implementation machinery were co-produced rather than substitutes.
cases.question: A high-level representation is semantically attractive but has not yet shown acceptable operational performance. What is the strongest next reachability move?

actions.A: Treat semantic elegance as sufficient evidence that implementation cost will be acceptable at scale.
actions.B: Build or access the complementary execution/optimization/recovery machinery and test whether it can honor the abstraction under target workloads and resources.
actions.C: Reject the representation solely because the first implementation is slower than a mature lower-level system.
actions.D: Standardize the surface globally before resolving whether any implementation can satisfy the required performance/recovery contract.

cases.terminal: The broadly standardized OSI protocol stack lost deployment to TCP/IP.
cases.lineage: The OSI trajectory is retained as a failure/parallel path: extensive international standardization did not guarantee deployment dominance. Practical outcome depended on deployability, existing network ecology, implementation timing, interoperability and lifecycle constraints. Standardization is a coordination carrier, not an automatic capability certificate.
cases.question: A formally broad standard exists, but a different ecosystem is winning practical deployment. What is the strongest reachability decision?

actions.A: Prefer the more formally comprehensive standard because institutional standardization proves it is the strongest practical carrier.
actions.B: Compare current deployability, installed ecology, interoperability, migration and lifecycle burden; treat the standard as one carrier rather than authority over practical reachability.
actions.C: Infer the standardized design is technically impossible because it lost deployment.
actions.D: Build a new universal stack rather than use either mature carrier.

cases.terminal: A modified-mRNA platform existed before its pandemic-scale payoff.
cases.lineage: The platform is retained as a delayed/dormant trajectory: an enabling scientific/technical basis can exist before the external target, manufacturing scale, delivery system, institutional funding, trial pathway and deployment conditions align. Dormancy does not equal current realized capability, but deleting the platform's reconstruction knowledge can destroy option value.
cases.question: A platform has no dominant current application but has source-grounded reusable capability and plausible future targets. What is the strongest persistence/reachability decision?

actions.A: Delete the platform and its reconstruction knowledge because no current large consumer exists.
actions.B: Preserve the cheapest trustworthy reconstruction/platform route and its prerequisites while allowing inactive instances to expire; revalidate when a concrete target appears.
actions.C: Keep all platform infrastructure permanently active because future uncertainty makes carrying cost irrelevant.
actions.D: Treat platform existence as proof that every future application is already path-qualified.

cases.terminal: LIGO produced the first direct gravitational-wave detection in 2015.
cases.lineage: Decades of interferometer development, vibration/isolation, laser stability, feedback/control, waveform modeling and geographically distributed detectors were required before the predicted phenomenon became directly observable. The transition created a new observational channel, not merely a more precise reading of an existing sensor.
cases.question: A phenomenon is theoretically well motivated but remains outside current observation capability. What is the strongest next reachability move?

actions.A: Increase confidence in the theory until the phenomenon can be treated as observed.
actions.B: Construct the missing observation/control/noise-rejection capability and independent cross-checks needed to make the phenomenon discriminable from rival/noise worlds.
actions.C: Treat current non-observation as proof that the phenomenon is physically impossible.
actions.D: Use one sensitive detector and infer target truth from any matching signal without independent noise/identity controls.

cases.terminal: NIF achieved target ignition/energy gain in 2022 and later repeated ignition with higher yield.
cases.lineage: Target ignition is a real experimental milestone after decades of experiments and near-misses, but it is not the same claim as a practical fusion-energy system. A system-level path still has different repetition-rate, driver efficiency, target production, materials, heat extraction, maintenance, economics and plant-integration obligations. Historical stage success must not be lifted into downstream realization.
cases.question: A decisive experiment establishes one important physical stage, while the ultimate system target remains unrealized. What is the strongest next reachability judgment?

actions.A: Promote the experimental milestone directly to current end-system capability because the central physical effect has been demonstrated.
actions.B: Preserve the stage success, then decompose and test the remaining system-level blockers rather than treating the experiment as terminal realization.
actions.C: Reject the physical-stage result because downstream engineering is incomplete.
actions.D: Assume repeated versions of the same experiment automatically discharge all downstream production/economic constraints.
